title: Sell Mineral Rights in Mammoth, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights near Mammoth, WY | Park County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights connected to the Mammoth area near Yellowstone in Park County, WY? Understand your options before assuming they're worthless.
heroLead: Mammoth sits inside Yellowstone National Park, which puts any mineral interest connected to this immediate area in a very different category than the rest of Park County.
intro: Federal park land isn't open to oil and gas leasing or development, period. If your family's paperwork references land in or immediately around Mammoth Hot Springs, the first question isn't what the minerals are worth, it's whether your interest actually sits inside the park boundary or in the surrounding national forest and private ground outside it.

sections.heading: Park boundary versus surrounding land
paragraphs: Yellowstone National Park's boundary is precisely mapped, and land immediately outside it, in Park County proper, follows the same Bighorn Basin oil and gas rules as the rest of the county. If your legal description places your interest outside the park, standard Park County valuation applies. Inside the park, mineral development isn't happening under current federal law.

sections.heading: Why some families still hold old paperwork here
paragraphs: Mineral deeds and reservations from before the modern park boundary was firmly settled sometimes still show up in old family paperwork, remnants of ownership claims that predate strict federal management. Sorting out whether such a claim has any current legal standing requires careful title and boundary work, not assumption either way.

sections.heading: What to do first
paragraphs: Confirm your exact legal description against the park boundary using Park County Clerk records in Cody. If your acreage sits outside the park in normal Bighorn Basin country, it can be evaluated like any other Park County mineral interest.

sections.heading: If your paperwork is genuinely unclear
paragraphs: Some families hold mineral paperwork referencing land near Mammoth that predates precise modern surveying, making the exact boundary relative to the park unclear without professional help. In that situation, a title professional or surveyor familiar with Park County and National Park Service boundary records is worth the investment before assuming either outcome.

faqs.question: Can minerals inside Yellowstone National Park be developed or sold for development value?
faqs.answer: No, federal law prohibits oil and gas leasing and development inside the park. Any interest confirmed to be inside the boundary has no development value under current law.

faqs.question: How do I know if my interest is inside or outside the park?
faqs.answer: Check your legal description's section, township, and range against the official park boundary, available through Park County Clerk records in Cody or National Park Service boundary maps.

faqs.question: What if my acreage is just outside the park boundary?
faqs.answer: It's treated like any other Park County Bighorn Basin mineral interest, evaluated on proximity to fields like Elk Basin, Oregon Basin, or Garland and current production status.

faqs.question: Who can help me determine if my old paperwork falls inside the park?
faqs.answer: A title professional experienced with Park County records, or the National Park Service's land boundary office, can help clarify exactly where an older legal description falls relative to the current park boundary.
